issues.legal_issue: An owner’s unequivocal decision to treat self-acquired property as joint family property can impress it with that character before a partition, even when the decision and partition occur close together.
material_facts: The owner executed a partition deed among himself and his children, who were represented by their mother.
The deed stated that the owner had blended his earnings and acquired property with inherited assets and treated the properties as joint family property.
The partition dealt with the self-acquired properties together with the inherited joint family property.
The court found that the partition proceeded on the basis that the self-acquired property was available for partition among the family members.
issues.conclusion: The deed evidenced an unequivocal decision to impress the self-acquired properties with the character of joint family property before the partition; the properties were then partitioned and held separately by the respective recipients.
issues.legal_principle: A person may, by an unequivocal act of volition, throw self-acquired property into the joint family stock. The deed may be evidence of that pre-existing decision, and the interval between the decision and partition need not be substantial. The court relied on the deed’s terms and the basis on which the partition proceeded.

predicates.family_partition_case: The dispute concerns a partition of property among members of a family.
predicates.owner_unequivocally_treated_self_acquire: The owner clearly chose to treat personally acquired property as property of the joint family.
predicates.partition_included_that_property: The property treated as family property was included in the partition among family members.

issues.definition: When a family partition includes self-acquired property that its owner unequivocally treated as family property, that property acquires joint family character before the partition.

issues.legal_issue: A genuine partition of property that had become joint family property is not a direct or indirect transfer of assets by the father to his minor children.
material_facts: The owner’s self-acquired properties were impressed with the character of joint family property before the partition.
The partition deed allotted shares among the owner and his minor children, who were represented by their mother.
The genuineness of the partition transaction was not in issue.
After the partition, the allotted properties were held separately by the respective recipients.
issues.conclusion: The partition deed did not amount to a direct or indirect transfer of assets to the minor children within the meaning of Section 16(3)(a)(iv) of the Income-tax Act, 1922.
issues.legal_principle: Section 16(3)(a)(iv) of the Income-tax Act, 1922 concerns direct or indirect transfers of assets to a minor child. Where property has become joint family property and is allotted to family members in a genuine partition, the partition is not such a transfer. The court followed Commissioner of Income Tax, Gujarat v. Keshavlal Lallubhai, [1965] 2 S.C.R. 99.

rule.if: tax_assessment_case and property_became_joint_family_property_before_partition and genuine_family_partition and minor_children_received_partition_shares

predicates.tax_assessment_case: The dispute arises in a tax assessment concerning whether assets allotted to minor children should be treated as transferred to them.
predicates.property_became_joint_family_property_be: The property acquired joint family character before the partition took place.
predicates.genuine_family_partition: The property was allotted in a genuine partition among family members.
predicates.minor_children_received_partition_shares: Minor children received shares of property under the family partition.

issues.definition: When property has become joint family property before a genuine family partition and minor children receive shares in that partition, the allotment is not treated as a transfer to them.

issues.legal_issue: An objection that a referred question should not have been answered cannot be raised for the first time at the Supreme Court stage when it was not raised before the High Court or in the statement of the case.
material_facts: The Revenue argued that a question referred to the High Court did not arise from the Tribunal’s order.
The Revenue had not raised that objection before the High Court or in the statement of the case before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The court did not allow the Revenue to raise the objection at that stage.
issues.legal_principle: The court declined to entertain an objection not raised before the High Court or in the statement of the case. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this procedural ruling.

predicates.appeal_or_reference_case: The matter reaches the Supreme Court through an appeal or a reference arising from an earlier court or tribunal proceeding.
predicates.objection_not_raised_before_high_court: The party did not raise the objection before the High Court.
predicates.objection_not_in_statement_of_case: The objection was not included in the statement of the case presented to the Supreme Court.

issues.definition: In an appeal or reference, an objection omitted both before the High Court and from the statement of the case is not entertained at the Supreme Court stage.
